correctness.rationale: Analytic incidence-count bound sum_a(rank_a−1)≤n(n−1). For n≤4 all stable matchings have minimum rank≤2; at n=5 the only exception has every agent at rank3 and is jointly optimal. In all remaining instances, a regret-minimizer with worst rank q has gap≤q−1, while every matching with worse worst rank has gap≥q−1, allowing joint optimization. For n=6, two structurally distinct exact enumerators verify all 720 perfect matchings, precisely seven stable outcomes, and disjoint unique minimizers; a separate all-46,656-profile n=3 regression passes. No finite test substitutes for the universal proof.

value.rationale: A source-motivated, independently natural pair of stability-constrained welfare objectives—protecting the worst individual versus minimizing interpersonal rank dispersion—has a sharp universal compatibility range. The analytic n≤5 guarantee eliminates a substantive social choice conflict for all markets up to that size, and the verified n=6 witness demonstrates the first genuine policy tradeoff. This is a structural universal theorem, not a routine extrapolation or arbitrary parameter slice.
